title: Round 10 / ECDLP-33: tightness of x-only interpolation degree bounds
question: Tightness conjecture for x-only interpolation: for E/F_p, P of prime order r and 2N < r, every g in F_p[X] with g(x(kP)) = k (resp. k^2) for 1 <= k <= N has deg g >= N − c for an absolute constant c (generic curves), improving the proven bound (N − 2)/3; or else there exist families with substantially lower-degree interpolants.
claims: L1 (proved, elementary): the minimal degree of g with g(x_k)=f(k), k<=N, equals max{j<N: c_j != 0} for the Newton divided differences c_j of f on the nodes x(kP); deficit N-1-mindeg is the length of the trailing zero run of c_j.

L2 (proved, elementary, not formalized): among translation-difference annihilators sum c_i G(Q+iP) (sum c_i=0, sum i c_i=0), support size s, width w, one gets N <= d*s + w, optimal at s=3,w=2, i.e. exactly Theorem C; the pole/zero-count method cannot beat alpha=1/3.

L3 (proved, not formalized): for anomalous j=0 curves over F_p, target k^2, N=(p-1)/2, the interpolant satisfies g(zeta X)=lambda^2 g(X), so g=X^s h(X^3) and deg g <= N-3+s; observed s=1 in 207/207 cases (deficit exactly 1; s=1 not proved). Hence mindeg=N-1 is not universal, but the deficit is O(1).

Experimental (finite, p<=997, 154288 cases, 162 primes): mindeg(N)<N-1 occurs for a fraction ~1/p of (curve,N), D>=2 ~1/p^2, max deficit 3, matching an independent-vanishing model outside small r, anomalous j=0 (L3) and some CM primes (p=19,79,109,167,269,383 for k^2 top level, unexplained). No lower bound deg g >= N-c or alpha>1/3 proved; conjecture C*: mindeg>=N-1-O(1) outside structured families is unproved.
next_action: Run the isomorphism-deduplicated histogram of deficits for p in [1000,5000] vs the 1/p model (minutes, tight.py); prove s=1 in L3; analyse small-degree CM endomorphism relations g∘R=mu^2 g at the top level (p=19,79,109,167,269,383) to see whether a deficit growing with N exists; have L1-L3 independently reviewed and (if kept) formalized in Lean.
